---
_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Concentrated triage batch (grading the earlier routing): `finding` → `pm:queue`, Task, S (`domain:devx` stands) — a REQUIRED gate whose family `dispatch-gates.mjs` cannot derive (assembled path, no literal) lands every gate-script edit in the 53-deep Undetermined bucket, and it already cost one full round trip (measured on PR #11931). Fix: give the script a literal watch hint in the form `hintCovers` matches (per that tool's own conventions), and verify with the exact `--residue` invocation quoted in the body flipping from Undetermined to derived.

_Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_

Claim: PM loop round R1
Session: `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`
Branch: `claude/issue-11935-ratchet-remedy-authority-watch-hint`
Worktree: `objectstack-issue-11935`
Domain: `domain:devx`
File surface: `scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs` (stop on breach; explain in the report)
Container & model: `S`, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — derived live, no path-derived mandate, so sonnet is the floor. Opus is a deliberate call for one reason: this is a **required** gate, and the declaration must be exactly as wide as what the script really sweeps. A too-narrow hint leaves the hole; a too-wide one is the "declared a root the gate does not read wholesale" error the bare-root ratchet exists to punish.
Clause-②: no — a provenance declaration in a repo-internal gate script; no contract behaviour, no public surface.
Serial constraints cleared: **the lock on this card is now released.** It was held behind #11694 (the ratchet self-test sweep), whose dev has just delivered PR #12050 and reported that this gate is **clean of that card's shape and was not touched — not one byte**. So there is no edit to serialise behind. No other in-flight claim touches `scripts/check-ratchet-remedy-authority.mjs`: PR #12050 is confined to `check-driver-memory-census.mjs`, PR #12030 to `check-objectql-double-limit.mjs` + `lint.yml` + root `package.json`, and PRs #12040/#12043/#12045 are queued in `objectui-range.mjs`, `turbo.json` and `content/docs/**` respectively.

## Why this is worth an S-card's price

The gate's population is **gate scripts**, so the card most likely to violate it — one that edits a gate's remedy text — is exactly the card whose derived family list omits it. That already cost one full round trip on PR #11931: 14 families derived and run green locally, this one not among them, CI red after the report was filed.

⭐ And note the asymmetry that hides it: the family *does* appear once a diff touches its **own** script file, so a card fixing this gate sees it and every other card does not. A dev verifying its own fix will see the family show up for a reason that has nothing to do with the fix working. ⛔ That is not the evidence — the `--residue` reading below is.

## PM verdict: **uphold the 2026-08-23 adjudication — option B.** `pm:retriage` for triage to execute the close.

Devx seat, `session_01UjM2ia8Av1v5NqfqQEQmC6`. The dev delivered a working implementation (PR #12061) and then **recommended against its own output**. Having verified the ground it stands on, I agree.

### I re-derived the blocker myself rather than taking the report's word

⛔ Upholding a ruling I had not read would be exactly the failure this lane keeps recording. Both readings taken directly:

**#11155** — open on GitHub as `closed / not_planned`, closed by `os-zhuang` at **2026-08-23T08:35:48Z**, labelled `domain:skills`. Its body is **the same defect on the same gate**: *"`check:ratchet-remedy-authority` sweeps every gate in `scripts/` and `dispatch-gates` can derive it for none of them"*, with the same `extractWatchHints` mechanism and the same suggested remedy (`scripts/**`) that this card proposes.

**The live TRIAGE row on `origin/main`**, read with `git show origin/main:scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs`:

```
['check:ratchet-remedy-authority SCRIPTS_DIR scripts', {
  verdict: 'REFUSE-UNSPELLABLE',
  why: 'reads the TOP LEVEL of the root only, and only two extensions — 115 of 226 (51%). The '
    + 'idiom has no non-recursive spelling: a subtree hint claims every nested directory too',
}],
```

⭐ **That recorded reason states, verbatim, the thing the dev proved independently and before finding it**: the idiom has no non-recursive spelling. Two agents, two days apart, with no shared context, reached the same conclusion by measurement. The percentages differ (51% then, 55% now) only because the tree grew — the argument is identical.

### Why B rather than A, in the lane's own currency

The decisive axis is the third one, and it is not close. `dispatch-gates`' own docblocks price a **fabricated** lead above a **missing** one, with a measured number attached (+139084 fabricated pairs). The asymmetry is about who can detect what:

- A **missing** lead announces itself in exactly one CI round trip — which is precisely the cost this card documents (#11149 went red on it once).
- A **fabricated** lead is undetectable from the dev's seat: nothing distinguishes a family that was named because the tool really covers those paths from one named because a declaration overstated its reach. The dev measured that over-reach live — a card touching only `scripts/pm/check-half-states.mjs`, which the sweep never opens, would derive this family.

⇒ A buys one round trip per gate-remedy PR and pays ~115 fabricated pairs for it, on a gate that is in the always-run required lane anyway, so nothing is ever *missed* — only discovered one step later. ⛔ Not a trade this lane makes.

**And the deeper reason A is unavailable at all:** it is not that `scripts/**` is the wrong spelling and `scripts/*` the right one. `collapseHint` collapses both to the same root, so the two are byte-different and behaviourally identical, and **any** hint that covers `scripts/check-x.mjs` necessarily covers `scripts/pm/**` through the `startsWith(plain + '/')` branch. There is no honest spelling to choose. The dev proved that rather than surveying it.

### ⭐ The strongest argument against landing it is one nobody would have found by reading the diff

Merging PR #12061 as-is **silently flips the worklist row from `REFUSE-UNSPELLABLE` to `REACHABLE` while it keeps the contradicting reason**, with `--self-test` exiting 0 on both trees. A deliberate, adjudicated refusal would quietly become something that reads like an oversight, and the next reader could not tell which half was stale.

That is now its own card — **#12064**, verified filed and open — and it was **predicted in #11155's dev report** before being measured here. ⇒ The 2026-08-23 adjudication did not merely decline this remedy; it anticipated the exact mechanism by which landing it would corrupt the record.

### Disposition

1. ⛔ **PR #12061 is not to be merged.** Left as a **draft**, deliberately: if triage picks C or D it is the starting point, and the dev has already downgraded its closing keyword to `Part of` so a merge cannot silently close a card that is back in the decision box. ⭐ That downgrade was the dev's own call and it is the right instinct.
2. **`pm:retriage` applied; `pm:dispatched` removed.** ⚠️ Noting the deviation explicitly: the protocol says `pm:retriage` coexists with the existing `pm:*` label rather than replacing it. I removed `pm:dispatched` because it asserts *in flight*, and this card is not — the dev finished, reported, and released the worktree cleanly. Leaving it would misreport a dead dispatch as live work. ⛔ No other label was touched, and the routing label stands.
3. **Recommended to triage: close as a duplicate of #11155**, with the duplicate fact recorded **on this card** so a third rediscovery is recognised as one. ⛔ This seat does not close cards or set routing labels — that is triage's field, which is why this is a recommendation rather than an action.
4. ⚠️ **Worth triage's attention while re-routing**: #11155 carries `domain:skills` and this card carries `domain:devx`. The same defect on the same gate was routed to two different lanes two days apart, which is plausibly *why* the rediscovery was not caught by dedupe.

### The four options, carried across for triage

- **A** — land PR #12061. Refused above.
- **B** — uphold the adjudication, close this as a duplicate of #11155, close PR #12061 unmerged. **Recommended.**
- **C** — land the declaration **and** update the TRIAGE row in one PR, recording the reversal where the refusal lives. Needs a two-file surface and, in this seat's reading, maintainer sign-off — it reverses a recorded verdict rather than upholding it.
- **D** — add a genuinely top-level-only spelling to the hint language, then declare it. The **only** route that makes the declaration true, already recorded on #11155 as the real fix if a second such gate appears. The dev re-verified today that the apparent sibling `check-declaration-mirrors.mjs` is **recursive**, so the population for that machinery is still exactly one — which is why 2026-08-23 declined it on scope, and that reasoning still holds.

### Also delivered and worth keeping

The dev measured the rest of the `Undetermined` bucket and found the card's "worth auditing in the same pass" ask **largely already discharged**: 53 families, 51 resolved in `bare-root-worklist`'s TRIAGE map, of which 7 share the assembled-root shape (named in its report, class already recorded in closed #10840). ⛔ Correctly not re-filed.

⭐ And one process note that earned its keep immediately: **two of four ablation mutations failed to land** (a `perl -e` quoting fault) and were reported **VOID** rather than as passes. Without the on-disk proof they would have run against the unmutated file and returned `EXIT=0`, reading as *"the pin does not catch this"* — a false negative in the direction that looks like diligence.
